title: Exterior sheaves commute with full-open restriction and pushforward
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $d\in\mathbf N$. Let $j:X|_X\to X$ be the inclusion of the full-open subscheme into $X$, and let $j^*M$ be the restriction of $M$ to that open subscheme. Writing $\bigwedge^d$ for the sheafification of sectionwise exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], there is an isomorphism of module sheaves $j_*(\bigwedge^d(j^*M))\cong\bigwedge^d M$. No local freeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$.

proof.text: The full-open inclusion j is the canonical scheme isomorphism X.topIso.hom. Its image and preimage operations on opens are inverse; they identify the structure sheaves, module restriction and pushforward, and covering families. Thus module sections and their scalar rings on corresponding opens are identified, compatibly with restriction.

On corresponding opens, use the exterior-power universal property to transport pure wedges through the section and scalar identifications. The inverse section identification gives the inverse exterior map. Both composites are identity on pure wedges, hence on every element since pure wedges span. Naturality follows by checking the two restriction composites on pure wedges using the characterized exterior restrictions. These maps give an isomorphism of exterior presheaves after transport through the equivalence of opens.

Transport the module-sheafification universal property through the equivalence of opens, which preserves covers. Given a map from the transported exterior presheaf to an X-module sheaf, restrict both target and map along j. The sheafification adjunction factors it uniquely through the exterior sheaf on the full-open subscheme. Pushing the factorization forward gives a unique factorization on X. Thus the pushforward of this exterior sheaf and exteriorSheaf M d are sheafifications of isomorphic exterior presheaves. Factor their two unit maps by these universal properties. Uniqueness makes the resulting maps inverse. For empty X all sheaves are zero; for d=0 the same construction uses the zeroth exterior power. No basis or local freeness is used.
